key_insight: SkeletonLLM converts structured, non-visual skeleton data into differentiable visual representations that MLLMs can directly understand, enabling end-to-end training and generalization across heterogeneous skeleton formats.
problem_solved: MLLMs cannot natively process structured motion/skeleton data; prior solutions either compress dynamics into lossy vectors or quantize motions into discrete tokens that fail to generalize across different skeleton formats and semantics.
method: Differentiable rendering: transform raw skeletons (varying joints/formats and temporal sequences) into canonical, learnable visual representations while keeping the pipeline differentiable.
MLLM integration: feed rendered visualizations into a pre-trained multimodal LLM to leverage its language-visual reasoning for tasks like description, querying, and editing.

End-to-end alignment & normalization: jointly optimize renderer and model with language supervision and format-agnostic normalization so the system generalizes across skeleton conventions and motion styles.
impact: Enables MLLMs to reason about and manipulate structured human-motion data without bespoke tokenization or format-specific encoders, simplifying workflows for action understanding, animation editing, human–robot interaction, and biomechanics research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: raw heterogeneous skeletons → differentiable renderer → rendered frames/heatmaps → MLLM → language/controls (include gradient arrows for end-to-end training).
Before/after comparison: (left) lossy vector or tokenized approaches vs (right) SkeletonLLM retaining structure and temporal dynamics.
Example gallery: rendered skeleton sequences with corresponding MLLM outputs (descriptions, queries, editing commands).
Generalization chart: bar/line chart showing cross-format performance and robustness gains vs prior methods.
paper_title: Universal Skeleton Understanding via Differentiable Rendering and MLLMs
paper_authors: Ziyi Wang, Peiming Li, Xinshun Wang, Yang Tang, Kai-Kuang Ma
